title: Batting Order as a Decision Tree: Who Should Delhi Capitals Promote and Why?
dek: Should Delhi Capitals write their batting order in ink or in pencil? How often their batters move positions shows how far they already treat it as a decision tree.
excerpt: Since 2024 Delhi Capitals' batting order has been about as flexible as the rest of the league's. The case for a flexible order rests on matching batters to the match situation.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

sections.heading: Ink or Pencil
body: A traditional batting order is fixed: each batter has a number. A decision-tree order uses triggers instead: if a wicket falls before the sixth over, send the anchor; if the platform is strong at the twelfth, send the hitter.
Since 2024 regular DC batters have each batted in {{ev:bo-t}} positions on average, against {{ev:bo-l}} for the rest of the league. Delhi Capitals' order has been about as flexible as the league's.

sections.heading: Who Moves
body: {{ev:bo-most}} has been the most mobile, batting in {{ev:bo-most-n}} positions. The table lists every regular batter by positions used.
Movement on its own is neither good nor bad: what matters is whether each move follows a rule the batters understand.

sections.heading: Building the Tree
body: The decision tree needs a few branches: wickets lost at the end of the powerplay, run rate at halfway, and the bowling still to come. Each branch names the next batter.
For DC, writing those triggers down before the season makes flexibility a plan rather than an improvisation.

sections.heading: The Cost of Uncertainty
body: Batters who do not know when they will bat can find it harder to prepare. Some evidence of that would show up as lower strike rates for batters who move often, but this analysis has not tested it.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: A Tree With Few Branches
body: Delhi Capitals should use a small number of clear triggers rather than a fixed order or constant improvisation.
Tracking each batter's output by position and by trigger would show which branches pay.
